title: The Iron Pillar That Won't Rust
description: Delhi's iron pillar has stood outdoors since the Gupta period with barely any rust.

scenes.narration: This iron pillar has stood outdoors for about sixteen hundred years, and it barely rusts.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient dark iron pillar standing in a courtyard of red sandstone ruins, Delhi

scenes.narration: It was made in the Gupta period, around 400 CE, probably under King Chandragupta the Second.
scenes.image_prompt: Gupta era Indian king in a royal court, 5th century, ornate jewellery

scenes.narration: It's over seven metres tall and weighs about six tonnes.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Indian workers raising a tall iron pillar with ropes and wooden frames

scenes.narration: Smiths forged it by hand, hammering together lumps of red-hot iron.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Indian blacksmiths hammering glowing iron in a forge, sparks flying

scenes.narration: Its iron is rich in phosphorus, which helps a thin protective layer form on the surface.
scenes.image_prompt: macro close up of smooth dark iron surface with inscriptions in ancient Brahmi script

scenes.narration: Today it stands in the Qutub complex in Delhi.
scenes.image_prompt: the Qutub Minar tower with the iron pillar in the foreground, blue sky

scenes.narration: For years, visitors tried to wrap their arms around it backwards for good luck.
scenes.image_prompt: visitors gathered around an ancient iron pillar in a courtyard, warm afternoon light

scenes.narration: Ancient Indian metalworkers were centuries ahead. What other ancient tech amazes you?
scenes.image_prompt: close view of the iron pillar top capital against a sunset sky
